summary: 一场风暴让人们发现石墨。它从给羊做记号的材料变成笔芯，经历木壳、配方和分级的改进，至今仍有用。

paragraphs.brief: 风暴刮倒大树，露出一种会在手上留下黑印的物质。
sentences: The history of the pencil starts with a violent thunderstorm.
铅笔的故事始于一场猛烈的雷暴。
When some particularly ferocious weather struck the Lake District in North West England in the sixteenth century, locals in the village of Borrowdale discovered a large uprooted tree.
16 世纪，一场格外猛烈的风暴袭击了英格兰西北部的湖区，博罗代尔村的居民发现一棵被连根拔起的大树。
Underneath the tree lay an unknown black substance which we now know as graphite, was slightly shiny and smooth to the touch.
树下有一种当时无人认识的黑色物质，略有光泽，摸起来很光滑。今天我们知道，那就是石墨。
And it left a black smear on the hands of all who touched it.
谁碰了它，手上都会留下一道黑印。

paragraphs.brief: 农民用石墨给羊做记号，后来人们把石墨包起来写字。
sentences: Initially, the local farmers used the newly discovered material as a handy way to identify their sheep.
起初，当地农民用这种新发现的材料给自家的羊做记号，十分方便。
However, others quickly realised the potential for using this intriguing substance to write on paper.
不过，很快就有人意识到，这种奇特的物质也可以用来在纸上写字。
When it was untreated the material was very soft, which meant that it was messy to handle.
未经处理的石墨很软，拿在手里容易弄得到处都是。
To make it fit for use with paper, people enclosed a thin core of the substance in stiff sheep hides or rope.
为了方便在纸上使用，人们用硬羊皮或绳子包住一根细细的石墨芯。
At this time chemistry was still in its infancy.
当时，化学还处于起步阶段。
People searched for a word to describe this increasingly useful substance and came up with plumbago which, in Latin, means acts or writes like lead.
这种材料越来越有用，人们为它取名 plumbago，这个拉丁词指的是“性质像铅，或写起来像铅”。
Later the name was changed to graphite.
后来，它改称 graphite（石墨）。
But because words have remarkable staying power, we still call graphite the lead of a pencil even though it is now known that there is no trace of real lead in graphite.
词语的生命力很强，即使如今人们已经知道石墨中没有一点真正的铅，仍然称铅笔里的石墨为 lead（铅芯）。

paragraphs.brief: 石墨的军事与商业价值引来政府接管，也催生盗窃与处罚。
sentences: Graphite has a very high melting point at around 3,500 degrees Celsius.
石墨的熔点很高，约为 3,500 摄氏度。
This made it invaluable to the British army and navy as a secret ingredient in the manufacture of cannon balls.
英国陆军和海军因而把石墨视为珍贵的材料，将其秘密用于制造炮弹。

The Royal Ordnance, or weaponry section of the British armed forces, used graphite as a lining inside the moulds for cannon balls, which, as a result, the British could turn out faster and more cheaply than their European rivals.
英国军队的军械部门将石墨用作炮弹铸模的内衬，因此英国生产炮弹的速度比欧洲对手更快，成本也更低。

In addition to its value to the armed forces, the government quickly realised the commercial potential of the graphite at Borrowdale, and assumed control of all the mines there during the sixteenth century.
除了石墨的军事价值，英国政府也迅速看到了博罗代尔石墨的商业潜力，于 16 世纪接管了当地所有矿场。
Armed guards accompanied the precious graphite all the way down to the metal foundries by the naval shipyards in the south of England.
武装卫兵一路押运珍贵的石墨南下，直到英格兰南部海军造船厂旁的金属铸造厂。
The graphite was so valuable that the locals, who called it wad, started to steal it.
石墨如此值钱，当地人开始偷取这种被他们称作 wad 的物质。
As a deterrent, an act of Parliament in 1752 made this offence punishable by time in prison.
为遏止盗窃，议会于 1752 年立法，规定偷窃石墨可判监禁。

paragraphs.brief: 意大利人发明木壳，德国人改进量产，法国人调整石墨与黏土的配方。
sentences: The Italians originally invented the wooden casing to hold a thin rod of plumbago firmly in place for ease of writing.
最早发明木制外壳的是意大利人，这种外壳能固定细石墨条，方便书写。
Italian craftsmen hollowed out two small sections of cedar wood, into one of which they laid the lead.
意大利工匠把两小块雪松木挖空，将笔芯放进其中一块。
They then glued the other section over the top and left the two halves to set.
他们随后把另一块盖上并粘合，再让两半静置定型。
When dry, the whole apparatus formed what today we know as a pencil.
胶干后，整个组合就成了我们今天所说的铅笔。
The Germans took this technique and developed it further by applying mass-production techniques to pencils.
德国人在此基础上进一步发展，把大规模生产技术用于铅笔制造。
At the same time Nicolas-Jacques Conté, a French officer in Napoleon Bonaparte’s army during the late 1700s, developed a method of mixing powdered graphite and clay together for firing in a kiln.
与此同时，18 世纪末在拿破仑军中服役的法国军官尼古拉-雅克·孔泰发明了一种方法，把石墨粉和黏土混合后送进窑里烧制。
Adding more clay to the mixture helped make the pencil harder, sharper, and more precise in its mark.
混合物中加入更多黏土，会让笔芯更硬、更尖，画出的线条也更精准。
More graphite helped make a pencil mark that was softer, thicker and darker.
更多的石墨则使笔迹更柔和、更粗、更深。

paragraphs.brief: 笔迹的差异促成了用 H 和 B 表示硬度与黑度的分级法。
sentences: The varying quality of pencil leads eventually gave rise to a system for categorizing the fineness of the pencil mark.
不同笔芯留下的笔迹各有特点，最终催生了一套区分笔迹细度的分级体系。
Pencil manufacturers all over the world still use this so-called HB grading system today.
时至今日，世界各地的铅笔制造商仍在使用这套所谓的 HB 分级体系。
The H stands for the Hardness of the pencil while the B stands for its Blackness.
H 代表硬度（Hardness），B 代表黑度（Blackness）。
An HB pencil is a standard pencil and a variety of letters and numbers are used to designate different types of lead.
HB 是标准型号，人们用不同的字母和数字标示其他类型的笔芯。

paragraphs.brief: 优质矿源逐渐耗竭，制笔业仍持续发展。
sentences: Significant seams of graphite exist in parts of China, which now produces most of the world’s pencils.
中国部分地区拥有储量可观的石墨矿脉，如今世界上大多数铅笔产自中国。
Interestingly, the Borrowdale mine in the Lake District remains the only significant source of graphite in its near-pure form in the world.
有意思的是，湖区的博罗代尔矿仍是世界上唯一能大量产出近乎纯净石墨的矿源。
Nowadays the highest grade of graphite at Borrowdale is totally exhausted, although other grades can still be found, and England’s pencil industry continues to thrive in the nearby town of Keswick.
如今博罗代尔最优质的石墨已经耗尽，但其他等级的石墨仍能找到，英格兰的铅笔工业也仍在附近的凯西克镇蓬勃发展。

paragraphs.brief: 作者借太空笔传闻说明铅笔在技术变迁中依然有用。
sentences: The pencil has turned out to be a remarkably resilient and valuable tool whose use has survived well into our high-tech times, as a well-known story shows.
一个广为人知的故事表明，铅笔经久耐用、价值不减，直到高科技时代仍有人使用。
It is sometimes said that the American space programme spent millions of dollars to invent a pen capable of writing in the zero gravity of space.
有一种说法是，美国航天计划花了数百万美元发明了一种能在太空失重环境中书写的笔。
The Russians, by contrast, simply equipped their astronauts with good old-fashioned pencils that never let them down.
据这则传闻，俄罗斯人干脆给宇航员配了可靠的老式铅笔。
It should be pointed out though, that the popular myth about Americans overlooking the practical advantages of pencils in zero gravity is merely fiction.
不过，所谓美国人忽略了铅笔在失重环境下的实用优势，纯属虚构。
In actual fact, both American and Russian astronauts were equipped with pencils in their respective countries’ first space flights.
实际上，美国和俄罗斯的宇航员在各自国家最初的太空飞行中都配备了铅笔。
A private company later developed pens for writing in zero gravity.
后来，一家私人公司研制出能在失重环境中使用的笔。
In fact, astronauts of every nation now use pens.
如今，各国宇航员都在使用这种笔。
But no matter — pencils remain in use in every classroom, every planning, building and drawing office, and in every art studio in the world.
不过铅笔仍活跃在世界各地的教室、规划设计室、建筑和制图办公室，以及艺术工作室。
And there is nothing to suggest that we are likely to invent anything better than graphite to use in our pencils.
也没有迹象表明，我们很可能发明比石墨更适合做笔芯的材料。

items.en: Graphite was first found below a ________ blown down in a storm.
items.zh: 石墨最初是在一棵被风暴刮倒的 ________ 下面发现的。
items.why: 风暴把树连根拔起。下一句的 Underneath the tree 承接树的位置。

items.en: The first use of graphite was to make marks on ________.
items.zh: 石墨最早被用来在 ________ 身上做记号。
items.why: 农民借这些记号辨认自家的羊。

items.en: Dirty to use because it is so ________.
items.zh: 天然石墨用起来容易弄脏手，因为它非常 ________。
items.why: 原文用 very soft 说明为什么拿在手里容易弄脏。

items.en: Originally wrapped in ________ or animal skin to make it useable as a pencil.
items.zh: 最初，人们用 ________ 或兽皮包住石墨，好用它写字。
items.why: 原文把两种材料写成 sheep hides or rope，题干把次序调换了。

items.en: The government completely took over the ________ at Borrowdale.
items.zh: 政府完全接管了博罗代尔的 ________。
items.why: all the mines 对应 completely took over 的范围，保留复数。

items.en: Local people began to ________ graphite for the money involved.
items.zh: 因为石墨值钱，当地人开始 ________ 石墨。
items.why: so valuable that 引出结果，当地人开始偷石墨。

items.en: The Italians were the first to make pencils out of wood.
items.zh: 意大利人最早用木头制作铅笔。
items.why: originally invented the wooden casing 说明木制笔杆最初由意大利人发明。

items.en: The Germans used different types of wood to produce pencils.
items.zh: 德国人用不同种类的木材制造铅笔。
items.why: 原文只交代德国人改进了批量生产技术，木材种类无从判断。

items.en: More clay in a pencil makes it write more darkly.
items.zh: 铅笔中黏土越多，写出的颜色就越深。
items.why: 增加黏土会使笔芯更硬。让笔迹更深的是增加石墨，题干把两种材料的效果调换了。

items.en: After the HB code was introduced, it very quickly became used by all manufacturers.
items.zh: HB 分级推出后，很快就被所有厂商采用。
items.why: 原文给出了今天的使用范围。推广花了多久没有交代，留意 very quickly。

items.en: English pencil factories have now all closed down.
items.zh: 英格兰的铅笔厂现在已经全部关闭。
items.why: 凯西克的铅笔工业仍然兴盛，足以推翻 all closed down。

items.en: American astronauts used pencils on their early journeys into space.
items.zh: 美国宇航员在早期太空飞行中使用过铅笔。
items.why: in actual fact 引出事实。美国和俄罗斯的宇航员在各自最初的太空飞行中都配备了铅笔。

items.en: The use of graphite pencils is unlikely to continue into the future.
items.zh: 石墨铅笔将来不大可能继续被使用。
items.why: 作者强调铅笔今天仍被广泛使用，也没有迹象表明会出现更好的笔芯材料。

pairs: 被风暴刮倒 ↔ 连根拔起
做标记的目的是辨认羊只
assumed control of all the mines
全面接管 ↔ 取得所有矿场的控制权
最早制作 ↔ 最初发明
早期太空旅行 ↔ 最初的太空飞行
points: 现在所有厂商都用 HB，只能确定今天的覆盖范围。很快普及是另一个需要证据的判断。
把 more clay 和 more graphite 分两行记。前者对应 harder，后者对应 darker。
clauses: which 回指前面“石墨质地很软”这件事，引出后果 messy to handle。
when 交代条件，先读“材料很软”，再接结果“容易弄脏”。
the highest grade … is totally exhausted / England’s pencil industry continues to thrive
although other grades can still be found 补充让步，限定耗尽的只是最高等级的石墨。
先找两个主要事实，再看 although 对适用范围的限制。
